v23_recovered_title: Graph-of-Context: Recoverable Fold/Unfold and Scoped Fork for Instrumented Long-Horizon Multi-Turn LLM Agentic Workflows
v23_abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents still tend to run long-horizon workflows as a single linear transcript. This representation is straightforward to implement, but it becomes brittle once a task spans many turns, tool outputs, updates, and late-binding pivots. We examine context management for an instrumented, single-session, long-horizon, multi-turn agentic workflow in which dependency links are available from workflow metadata, tool logs, citations, or controller annotations, and introduce Graph-of-Context (GoC) as a split between a recoverable storage graph and a budget-constrained active context. GoC is built around three recoverable operators: fold, which compresses inactive episodes into proxy nodes in the active view while preserving the original subgraph in storage; unfold, which restores a budget-feasible dependency-supporting subgraph at expensive checkpoints; and scoped fork, which creates a temporary least-privilege view for a specialist sub-agent and rejoins the result with explicit provenance edges. We formalize the storage graph, active-context construction, dependency closure, fork-time projection, and rejoin procedure. In LLM-based TraceOps experiments with gpt-4.1-mini, the validated fold/unfold core raises delayed-activation decision accuracy from 25.0% to 42.5%, cuts mean prompt tokens by 54%, and reduces over-commitment from 0.625 to 0.340. A deterministic selector study then isolates fork scope quality: in the mismatch setting ( $d=6$ ), dependency-scoped fork reaches the full-context performance upper bound at roughly one-third of the token cost and surpasses similarity-scoped fork under a matched token budget. A limited end-to-end workflow validation further shows that fork alone is not sufficient, but that a mixed graph-native policy can match full-history prompting accuracy (0.396) while reducing mean prompt tokens from 49.1k to 38.1k and median prompt tokens from 69.2k to 35.6k. Workflow-level comparisons show that graph-native policies improve over similarity-only retrieval and proxy summarization in long-horizon support restoration, and failure/sensitivity analyses identify remaining error sources. In a six-seed dependency perturbation study, closure-only restoration changes from 0.368 at baseline to 0.340 under 30% edge removal and 0.347 under 20% noisy-edge injection; the Mixed-Heuristic policy retains higher absolute accuracy across the same conditions (0.493, 0.493, and 0.465, respectively). Overall, the results support a focused claim: GoC introduces recoverable, graph-native context management for instrumented single-session workflows with available or constructible dependency traces, and scoped fork adds dependency-aware projection with provenance-preserving rejoin within that trace graph.

v23_recovered_title: Entitlement-Aware Authorization for MCP-Based AI Search and Chat Systems
v23_abstract: Large-language-model (LLM) agents increasingly reach enterprise data through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). MCP standardizes how a model discovers and invokes tools exposed by back-end systems, but not who may invoke which tool on whose behalf, nor which rows they may receive in the response. This paper defines an entitlement-aware authorization architecture for MCP, a first-class Policy Decision Point (PDP) and per-tool Policy Enforcement Points (PEPs) sit between the AI orchestrator and the back-ends, consume the end-user’s attested identity and attributes, produce obligations that narrow returned rows, and record every decision in a unified audit stream. The design composes with OAuth 2.1, OIDC, and JWT infrastructure and with the three common MCP-to-back-end integration patterns (service-account, token-passthrough via OAuth Token Exchange, and per-user credentials). AI orchestrator that can invoke MCP tools against multiple enterprise back-ends is prevented from leaking sensitive data by an externalized, identity- and attribute-aware authorization layer.

title: Containing the Cascade: A Benchmark and Reference Mediator for Failure Propagation in Tool-Using LLM Multi-Agent Systems

v23_recovered_title: Containing the Cascade: A Benchmark and Reference Mediator for Failure Propagation in Tool-Using LLM Multi-Agent Systems
v23_abstract: Large language model (LLM) multi-agent systems (MAS) increasingly automate multi-step, tool-using workflows, yet they fail far more often than their single-agent counterparts. Recent diagnostic studies attribute these failures to cascades: a single agent’s hallucination, malformed tool call, or role drift propagates through the agent graph and corrupts the final output. The community has so far concentrated on diagnosing such failures after the fact; there is no standard, reproducible benchmark for measuring whether a system can contain a cascade as it unfolds. We address this gap with three contributions. First, we introduce a taxonomy of six recurring cascading-failure modes and a suite of containment metrics—containment rate, cascade depth, blast radius, and mean time-to-detection—that quantify propagation rather than only end-task success. Second, we present Cascade-Bench, a controlled fault-injection testbed of 1080 scenarios across six task domains, instantiated on a discrete-event simulation of agent message passing that is calibrated to reported MAS failure statistics. Third, we propose Sentinel, a lightweight reference mediator that combines typed inter-agent message contracts, a semantic anomaly gate, a circuit breaker, and checkpoint-based recovery. Across 48 system configurations and over 590000 simulated task executions, Sentinel raises task success from 31.3% to 83.7% and containment from 46.2% to 99.4%, while holding cascade depth nearly constant as the system scales from 3 to 12 agents—where the unguarded depth nearly doubles. An ablation cleanly separates a fail-safe role (the circuit breaker, which governs containment) from a fail-operational role (checkpoint rollback, which governs task completion). We release Cascade-Bench and Sentinel as an open baseline for reliability research on tool-using MAS.

v23_recovered_title: CloudHeal: LLM-Driven Fault Self-Healing in Aerospace Cloud Platforms via Structured Recovery Knowledge
v23_abstract: As aerospace missions increasingly rely on cloud-native infrastructure for measurement, launch, and control (MLC) services, the need for autonomous fault recovery has become critical. This paper presents CloudHeal, an LLM-driven self-healing agent framework designed for containerized cloud platforms. We propose a structured recovery knowledge architecture that organizes fault-handling experience into three layers—recovery strategies, repair routines, and command-level operations—enabling systematic reuse of diagnostic and repair experience across heterogeneous fault scenarios. An automatic knowledge acquisition module distills and refines recovery procedures from successful healing trajectories, enabling continuous self-improvement. We evaluate CloudHeal on a containerized cloud testbed deploying representative MLC microservices. Experimental results demonstrate that CloudHeal achieves 91.0% recovery success rate with an average of 8.5 steps, outperforming platform-native self-healing (16.0% success) and manual recovery (78.0% success, up to 15.2 minutes) by a significant margin.

v23_recovered_title: A Semantic-Constraint-Driven Agent Decision Framework for Self-healing of Distribution Networks
v23_abstract: During distribution network self healing, operators often issue or receive operating requirements expressed in natural language, such as maintaining the supply of critical loads, prohibiting the restoration of specific loads, and forbidding the closure of specific switches. Existing restoration models, however, usually rely on structured inputs and therefore cannot respond to semantic constraints in an explicit and consistent manner. To address this issue, this paper proposes an agent framework for self healing driven by semantic constraints and develops a decision workflow that integrates semantic parsing, constraint mapping, restoration solving, independent safety verification, and closed loop correction. The proposed method converts natural language dispatch requirements into structured constraints and further injects them into the action space and solution process of self healing decision models, thereby enabling a stable and operationally meaningful transfer from semantic constraints to restoration actions. Experiments on the IEEE 13 bus system show that the proposed framework effectively responds to several typical dispatch requirements and further improves the safety, operational feasibility, and interpretability of restoration results. These results provide a practical new approach to semantic interaction and human machine collaborative decision making in distribution network self healing.

v23_recovered_title: Securing Autonomous Clinical Agents: Time-Scoped Hypergraph Delegation for Controlling Patient Data Access
v23_abstract: Healthcare data breaches cost hospitals and clinics an average of $7.42M USD per breach. Autonomous multi-agent LLM pipelines in clinical settings multiply that exposure structurally: a prompt-injection payload embedded in a laboratory report or referral note traverses the full delegation hierarchy before any human reviewer observes it. Standard mechanisms including flat Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Macaroon caveat chains provide no structural guarantee that a spawned sub-agent's permissions remain bounded by its parent's scope. The Minimum Necessary Standard must hold across mixedsensitivity EHR data and multi-hop chains simultaneously. That is, the gap is architectural, not behavioral. We present the Hybrid Scripted-Execution and Prompt-Grounded Injection (SEPI) design, a replay-faithful methodology that freezes authorizationrequest traces and replays them identically across baselines to isolate authorization semantics from LLM stochasticity. Applied to a five-agent post-surgical oncology coordination workflow over a synthetic Electronic Health Record scenario, and evaluated against 39 clinically grounded injection payloads across leafagent, mid-delegate, and parent-orchestrator compromise scenarios, NGAC-hypergraph time-scoped delegation reduces mean sensitivity-weighted blast radius $\left(B_{\mathrm{w}}\right)$ by 75.0% relative to flat RBAC and 65.2% relative to Macaroon caveat chains. A temporal ablation shows that removing $t_{\text{expire }}$ raises mean $B_{\mathrm{w}}$ by 75.0% relative to full NGAC. The reduction follows from structural properties of the delegation architecture: attenuation is provable by construction rather than contingent on model behavior. Across model conditions, Claude Sonnet 4.6 actively detected all 39 payloads while open-source models showed weaker or intermittent behavioral protection, reinforcing authorization as the model-agnostic containment control.

v23_abstract: Cloud-edge computing environments are evolving rapidly, requiring orchestration mechanisms that may automatically construct and manage complex multi-step workflows with little human intervention. We introduce a framework for the agentic AI and how it should be able to orchestrate an autonomous end-to-end workload of cloud-edge enterprise infrastructures in general. The proposed framework relies on large language model (LLM)-driven agents capable of dynamic task decomposition, real-time decision-making, and self-correcting execution pipelines to manage heterogeneous workloads. Through the incorporation of multi-agent coordination protocols, context-aware scheduling algorithms, and feedback-driven optimization loops, the system facilitates seamless task delegation throughout edge nodes and cloud backend systems while managing latency, resource allocation, and compliance constraints. Experimental evaluations show up to percentage improvements in workflow completion rates, resource utilization, and fault tolerance over traditional static-command Rule-based orchestration approaches. Additionally, the framework features explainability modules and audit trails to promote transparency and accountability in autonomous operations. The results provide evidence that agentic AI architectures can serve as a scalable, resilient and intelligent control mechanism for next generation enterprise workflow management across hybrid cloud-edge settings. This has laid a foundation and is to our best of knowledge, the first systematic pioneers work that lays down a roadmap for production-grade autonomous orchestration deployed in analytics and enterprise domains.

v23_recovered_title: Autonomous Agentic AI for Self-Defending and Self-Recovering Cloud Infrastructure
v23_abstract: The modern digital services rely upon cloud computing, which is scalable, flexible, and cost-effective. Nevertheless, the common and dynamic infrastructure it has puts it at risk of more advanced cyber attacks, service attacks, and insider attacks requiring smart autonomous defense measures. The old form of security systems such as the conventional intrusion detection systems (IDS) are not able to identify the complex attacks in real-time and in most cases, they are not able to recover without a lot of human involvement resulting in downtime and loss of data. This paper aims to solve these problems by presenting an Autonomous Agentic AI platform of self-defense and self-healing cloud infrastructure. The suggested framework combines a spatial attention (SAtt) mechanism with quantum convolutional neural network (QCNN) to identify threats in a precise and fast way due to the focus on the crucial network features, whereas an improved Hungarian optimization (EHO) algorithm determines the best defensive actions and reallocation of resources. The samples of data of CICIDS2017 and NSL-KDD datasets are preprocessed to eliminate noise and normalize the distribution of features and Adaptive Synthetic (ADASYN) sampling is used to address class imbalance. Experiments show that the suggested A3I framework has 99.85% accuracy on CICIDS2017 and 99.42% accuracy on NSL-KDD, which is 1 percent more accurate than the state-of-the-art deep learning IDS models, as well as 32% shorter on average recovery time than the traditional automated recovery software.

v23_abstract: Tracking dynamic entity states across open-domain sources faces significant challenges, including noise interference, heterogeneous data integration, and evolving entity profiles. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel framework powered by Large Language Model (LLM) Agents for automated, accurate, and adaptive entity dynamic tracking. The framework integrates three core innovations: (1) A two-stage disambiguation mechanism combining rule-based filtering with LLM Agentdriven verification to precisely isolate target entities from noisy web content; (2) An LLM-based extraction module that uniformly structures events, achievements, and state changes from heterogeneous sources; (3) A hybrid event-processing strategy leveraging semantic vector retrieval and LLM Agent reasoning to deduplicate information and model state evolution. By orchestrating LLM Agents for contextual decision-making-such as tool-augmented identity validation and event fusion-the system constructs dynamic entity profiles while minimizing redundancy. This work bridges LLM capabilities with dynamic knowledge tracking, providing a scalable solution for open-domain entity surveillance.

v23_recovered_title: Intent-Driven Autonomous Reconfiguration for Telecom OSS: A Generative-AI-Empowered Hierarchical Multi-Agent Architecture
v23_abstract: Telecom Operation Support Systems (OSS) still depend on domain experts and ad-hoc scripts for network and service reconfiguration, a process that is labor-intensive, errorprone, and fragile whenever cross-domain dependencies-such as allocating an IP address before tearing down a VLAN—must be respected. The heterogeneity and dynamism anticipated for 6Gclass networks only magnify the shortcomings of today’s rigid, rule-based automation pipelines. This paper introduces an intent-driven, fully autonomous reconfiguration framework that integrates Generative AI with a hierarchical Multi-Agent architecture. At its core, a ReWOOenhanced Chief Agent transforms natural-language intents into a dependency-aware execution graph, utilizing a formally defined Command Pattern to explicitly specify actions and associated data for unambiguous inter-agent coordination. Atomic tasks-annotated with domain-specific constraints and keys governed by a Primary Key Pattern-are delegated to ReAct-based Specific Agents responsible for IP management, network control, cloud orchestration, and service management. Evaluation on a four-domain OSS testbed exposing over thirty RESTful APIs confirms accurate intent parsing, robust key-value consistency enforcement, strict adherence to create-before-destroy constraints, and seamless scalability from single-domain provisioning to complex cross-domain orchestration without code changes. The proposed work delivers a reusable agent blueprint decoupling global planning from domain execution; formal interagent interfaces curbing hallucination and enabling modular growth; an execution-aware extension to ReWOO for structured action planning; domain-driven guidelines for encapsulating OSS subsystems into loosely coupled agents; and a public OSS testbed for benchmarking future Agentic-AI architectures-collectively advancing OSS reconfiguration toward scalable, maintainable, and 6G-ready network operations.
